title: Partial output finalizers, resumable tokens, and backpressure protocol for disconnected clients
creator: Asha Patel
body:
Summary:
We need a robust protocol and server-side finalization/cleanup model for streaming generations when clients disconnect, exceed timeouts, or partially consume output. Current behavior leaves ephemeral partial outputs in the cache and can result in stale/inaccessible artifacts, uneven resource usage, and customer-facing surprise (partial tool calls or incomplete structured outputs). This ticket proposes: 1) a resumable resume-token model for reconnects, 2) a server-side 'finalizer' event that collapses partial generations into a compact tombstone or persisted artifact, and 3) a credit-based backpressure upgrade to reduce orphaned in-flight work.

Problem statement and pain points:
- Clients disconnect mid-stream (network flaps, mobile suspend) and may reconnect expecting to resume but current resume semantics are ad-hoc and inconsistent across clients.
- Partial tool/function calls risk being left halfway (e.g., tool invoked but callback never attached), leading to side-effect confusion.
- Long-lived partial KV cache state increases memory/GPU residency and skews batching heuristics.
- Operators see spikes in 'orphan generations' and higher than expected token billings without corresponding completed responses.

Goals:
- Provide a deterministic reconnect/resume flow with a short-lived resume token that guarantees idempotent resume or clear finalization.
- Emit a server finalizer artifact on disconnect or timeout that is safe for downstream evaluation, tooling, and audit logs.
- Enforce backpressure via a credit window per-client and per-session to bound outstanding tokens and prevent runaway resource retention.
- Make behavior observable in Console (orphaned_count, avg_orphan_lifetime, resume_success_rate) and alertable when thresholds crossed.

Proposed design (high level):
1) Resume tokens and session leases:
   - Every streaming session issues a resume_token in the initial response metadata. Token TTL = 90s (configurable per-customer).
   - Resume uses a Resume-Token header + last-ack-offset to reattach. If token expired, client gets HTTP 410 with guidance to re-issue request.
   - Tokens are single-resume (one successful resume) to avoid concurrent resumes; second attempt returns 409 Conflict.

2) Finalizers and tombstones:
   - On explicit client close (well-formed close frame) server attempts graceful finalization: run structured-output validation and produce a compact final artifact stored in ephemeral store with TTL 24h.
   - On abrupt disconnect or token expiry, server runs a deterministic finalizer: summarize last delta, annotate tool calls as 'aborted' and generate a tombstone JSON capturing last-valid-state + reason (client_disconnect, timeout, reclaim).
   - Finalizer artifacts surface to Console under request trace and are linkable to PRDs/incident pages.

3) Credit-based backpressure (per-session):
   - Implement a token-credit window: client may request up to N outstanding tokens (default 4) per streaming session. Server will queue/hold further tokens at ingress until downstream batch/execution resources free up.
   - Credits decrement when server begins work on a response chunk and increment when an ACK or finalizer runs.
   - For long-running chains with tool calls, we add an additional 'side-effect credit' that must be consumed before invoking irreversible operations; if absent, server returns a 429-streaming-credit-exhausted code prompting client to throttle or convert to non-streaming request.

4) Tool/function calling semantics on disconnect:
   - Tool invocations enter a two-phase state: invoked -> awaiting-callback. If client disconnects before callback attachment, the finalizer either: (a) re-run the tool under a 'dry-run' cap and attach a neutral result, or (b) mark the invocation as 'aborted' and emit structured placeholder. Determination made by tool idempotency metadata provided at model onboarding.

5) Observability and telemetry:
   - New metrics: orphaned_generations_count, orphaned_generation_duration_seconds (histogram), resume_tokens_issued, resume_success_rate, credits_blocked_total.
   - Console: per-model and per-key dashboard panels, alerts for orphaned_generation_rate > 1% sustained and resume_success_rate < 80% across 5m.

6) UX and API surface changes:
   - Resume-Token header returned in initial stream and finalizer events include finalizer_url.
   - Error codes: 410 ResumeTokenExpired, 409 ResumeConflict, 429 StreamingCreditExhausted, 424 FinalizerPending (for clients awaiting finalization).

Acceptance criteria:
- reconnect/resume flow covered by e2e tests (simulated disconnect, resume within TTL, assert state continuation).
- finalizer artifacts generated for abrupt disconnects and visible in Console traces.
- credit window prevents >N active generation tasks per-session in stress tests.
- automated migration runbook and a failing-on-high-orphan alert created in PagerDuty.

Rollout plan:
- Phase 1 (canary): runtime-1.20-canary with credit window default disabled and resume-token support enabled (server logs resume token events). 1-week canary on internal org + selected beta customers.
- Phase 2: enable credit window default for new keys; console telemetry added. Monitor metrics for 2 weeks.
- Phase 3: enforce tokens TTL and tombstone finalizers; notify customers via console and changelog.

Testing plan:
- Unit tests for token lifecycle, credit accounting, and finalizer generation.
- Integration test matrix: abrupt TCP disconnect, HTTP/2 GOAWAY, mobile suspend (app background), and client forced 429 handling.
- Load test with synthetic clients to validate memory/GPU residency under high churn.

Artifacts:
- Confluence design: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/RT/pages/22440123/partial-output-finalizers (draft)
- Reference PR (runtime): https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/7124 (WIP)
- Test harness (internal): gs://redwood-test-harness/streaming-resume/2025-02

Open questions / trade-offs:
- TTL values: 90s token TTL vs. user convenience for mobile reconnections (trade-off between resource holding and UX).
- Tool re-run policy: safe for purely functional tools but risky for side-effectful tools; need tooling metadata to mark tool idempotency.
- Persistence boundary: keep finalizers in ephemeral store (24h) vs. writing to longer-term audit logs for compliance customers.

Next steps:
- Finalize API error codes and header names (deadline 2025-02-14).
- Engineering spike to prototype credit window (2d) and finalize metric names (2025-02-12 to 2025-02-14).
- Submit PR for resume-token plumbing and a simple tombstone generator (target PR by 2025-02-18).
